title: Child care is getting in the way of work
summary: Help parents find care that fits the hours they actually work.
evidence: Baltimore’s 2025 early childhood landscape analysis describes child care disrupting work and education among families in the Baltimore Young Families Success Fund study. This is evidence from that study, not a measure of every family in the city.
ideas: An employer and provider care pilot

Bring a local employer and a licensed child care provider together to test whether a small block of funded care hours fits parents’ shifts. Establish staffing, licensing and costs with the provider before offering places.
Help families use existing referral services, record where the search breaks down, and share verified availability with permission. Build a new tool only if existing services cannot address the gap.
first: Speak with five parents about the last time care disrupted work. Ask whether cost, opening hours, location or availability was the deciding barrier. Do not assume all four need the same solution.
people: Parents, licensed providers and an employer in one Baltimore neighborhood.
measure: Whether participating parents find suitable care and report fewer shifts missed because of care.

title: Small businesses struggle with uneven cash flow
place: Maryland · start with a local business group
summary: Help owners understand what is coming in, what is due and where payments get stuck.
evidence: In the Federal Reserve’s 2025 Maryland employer-firm chartbook, 51% of respondents reported uneven cash flow as a financial challenge. The survey does not establish late invoices as the cause or describe every Maryland business.
source: Federal Reserve Banks, 2025 Maryland employer-firm chartbook
ideas: Work with a business association and a qualified adviser to help owners build a simple weekly cash forecast. Test whether a shared spreadsheet and a regular check-in are enough.
If interviews identify overdue invoices as a recurring cause, pilot clearer payment terms, reminders and an invoice tracker with willing owners. Compare existing tools before developing software.
first: Ask five owners in one commercial district what caused their most recent cash shortfall. Separate weak sales, seasonal demand, expenses and delayed payments before choosing a project.
people: Business owners, a local merchants association and an experienced bookkeeper or SBDC adviser.
measure: Whether owners can identify upcoming shortfalls earlier and spend less time chasing payments. Do not promise increased revenue.
keywords: founder startup cashflow invoices money business

title: Professional experience does not always lead to a matching job
place: Maryland · test one profession in one community
summary: Help internationally trained residents navigate credentials and local career pathways.
evidence: Maryland’s Skilled Immigrant Task Force identifies costly credential evaluations, complex licensing, limited professional networks and unfamiliar career pathways as barriers. These statewide observations do not tell us which barrier matters most in a particular community.
source: Maryland Department of Labor, Skilled Immigrant Task Force
ideas: A verified guide for one profession
Work with the relevant licensing board and a workforce adviser to explain one profession’s requirements, official fees and routes. Assign someone to review the guide when requirements change.
Connect willing professionals with trained advisers and peers in the same field. Begin with a small, facilitated session to identify missing information and useful introductions.
first: Choose one profession. Interview five internationally trained residents and a workforce adviser about where the process stalls. Check whether an existing program already covers that need.
people: Internationally trained residents, workforce advisers, professional associations and the relevant licensing board.
measure: Whether participants understand their next verified step and complete it. A checklist cannot waive licensing rules or guarantee employment.
keywords: immigrant credentials career job employment training
